title: Hosted API Model Rollback Runbook
author: Hannah Schmitt
body:
h1. When to use this
Use this runbook when a new Hosted API model version causes a production regression or violates rollout gates during a rollout.

h1. Immediate actions (first 5 minutes)
# Stop the ramp. Do not continue increasing traffic.
# If customer impact is ongoing, declare an incident following the Incident Process.
# Move routing weight for the new version to 0% for the affected route.
# Confirm fallback points to last-known-good and that fallback is not rate-limited.

h1. Verification steps
After setting weight to 0%:
* Confirm traffic split is 0% new version across all regions.
* Confirm error rate and latency return toward baseline.
* Confirm streaming disconnect rate returns toward baseline.
* Confirm runtime error logs stop emitting the new regression signature.

h1. If rollback does not mitigate
If customer impact persists after traffic is removed:
* Verify the stable version is healthy (no unrelated incident).
* Check for config changes shipped alongside the rollout (gateway timeouts, batching settings).
* Consider moving the route to an alternate stable version if the current stable is also degraded.
* Escalate to eng-serving-runtime and eng-infra if saturation persists.

h1. Capture evidence
The driver MUST capture in the tracking ticket:
* exact time of rollback
* dashboards showing gate violation
* error samples (request IDs, error codes)
* version IDs: canary and stable

h1. Communication
Follow the Hosted API model rollout communications playbook. Minimum requirement:
* internal update in #eng-releases and #eng-oncall
* if customer-visible: notify #support and update status page if impact meets criteria

h1. Next steps
* File a follow-up task to root-cause and fix before attempting re-rollout.
* If rollback was triggered by a quality regression, attach eval evidence and prompt-set IDs used.
* If rollback was triggered by perf regression, attach perf-canary comparison output and runtime profiling notes.
